text:
rachel: FYI customer 'AcmeRetail' pinged Support — p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms -> ~820ms after the 03:14 deploy in us-west1. They see very spiky latencies and some 5xxs. Suspect KV/prefix cache warmup thrash. Adding logs + traces below.

devin: Can you paste a minimal repro and the model/route they hit? Also which pool (dedicated/shared)?

rachel: route: POST /v1/generate model: redwood-13b-v2 pool: shared-us-west1 tenant: acme-retail workload is short prompts (avg 30 tokens) but high QPS ~45/s. Repro: quick curl we got from them: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"Price for item 123?","max_tokens":40}'
```
They also attached trace ids: trace: trc_0a9f... and logs show repeated cache-miss flood.

maria: I pulled infra metrics — KV miss-rate for the tenant spiked to 92% between 03:15-03:20 and eviction rate doubled. Heap of runtime instances showing TTL-driven evictions. Heatmap attached (summarized): hot prefixes shifted rapidly, high key-cardinality due to session-id header leak.

jin: quick grep of logs for tenant -> found this pattern of dynamic user session prefixes being used as cache keys (headers x-session-id included in prefix key). Looks like our prefix canonicalization didn't strip ephemeral header in the new rollout: 
```text
2026-03-12T03:16:02Z runtime DEBUG prefix_key="user:session:8e7f3a4b" miss=true
2026-03-12T03:16:02Z runtime DEBUG prefix_key="user:session:2c9b1f7d" miss=true
```
That explains the explosion of unique keys.

sam: Repro locally: I ran a small script hitting shared-us-west1 with rotating X-Session-Id — reproduced p95 from 90ms -> 780ms on our staging runtime with KV miss multiplier. Script: 
```python
for i in range(1000):
  headers = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer X', 'X-Session-Id': str(uuid4()) }
  post('/v1/generate', headers=headers)
```
If you strip X-Session-Id from prefix calculation p95 stays ~120ms.

devin: OK this looks like a regression in prefix normalization code path from the deploy. @maria can you confirm rollout version for shared-us-west1? Any correlation with canary?

maria: Rollout 2026.03.12-03:12 — yes, canary finished around 03:13. Metrics show the miss-rate jump coincides with that rollout. Canary didn't trigger alerts.

opsbot: [ALERT] KV miss-rate threshold breached for pool shared-us-west1 (tenant acme-retail) — triggered at 2026-03-12T03:15:10Z. Incident created: INC-6523.

rachel: Customer is asking for ETA / workaround. They're on shared but this affects their latency SLO. We need either rollback, quick mitigation, or per-tenant warmup.

jin: Immediate mitigation options (fast -> slow):
- rollback the prefix-normalization change (fast if we can block deployments)
- add a hot-prefix canonicalization blacklist (strip session-like headers) with a config flip on edge (fast, low-risk)
- enable small KV warmup grace window: treat first N requests for a prefix as non-evictable for 30s (medium)
- change eviction to LFU for 5m window for shared pool (risky)

devin: I can push a config flip to strip X-Session-Id from prefix keys for shared-us-west1 in ~15-20m. That should collapse cardinality quickly. Rollback is also possible but would be heavier.

maria: As a quick band-aid I can also increase the per-shard cache size for shared-us-west1 by 10% to absorb the spike while the fix deploys. That buys like 10-15m headroom.

sam: Confirmed that with header stripped locally p95 returns to normal. Good to go.

rachel: I'll coordinate comms with Support: telling customer we're aware, mitigation in progress (canonicalization flip + shard bump). Ask them to avoid rotating session header for now if possible.

devin: Action items:
- devin: flip header-canonicalization blacklist for shared-us-west1 (in 15m) [ETA 03:40]
- maria: increase cache shard size by 10% (immediate)
- jin: prepare rollback PR if flip doesn't help (reviewer: devin)
- rachel: send customer update citing INC-6523 and ETA

maria: I'll also schedule follow-up postmortem to validate test coverage for header->prefix mapping and add a canary probe that exercises prefix key cardinality.

rachel: Customer reply: "appreciate the quick response, please keep us posted" :thumbsup:

opsbot: [INC-6523] status: mitigation_in_progress -> monitoring.

devin: After flip we'll monitor p95/p99 and KV miss-rate. If miss-rate drops and p95 normalizes we'll keep the change and roll a more robust fix in next patch.

jin: Long-term: add a normalization whitelist/blacklist per-tenant + unit tests that simulate header explosion (randomized prefixes) so this doesn't regress. Also consider sticky-prefix warmup heuristics keyed by tenant.

rachel: Note for follow-up: tie this to SLA investigation for AcmeRetail and include billing impact calc (they had retries). I'll open a bill-impact ticket.

sam: great, thanks everyone. I'll help with quick e2e test for the flip.

(dev thread ends)
